items.headline: At least 68 killed as high-speed trains collide in Spain
items.summary: A high-speed train slammed into another train stopped on the tracks south of Madrid, in Spain's second deadly rail collision this year. The transport minister blamed the crash on an 'inexplicable' error.

items.headline: Fed holds rates steady as inflation stays stubborn
items.summary: The Federal Reserve left its benchmark rate unchanged at Chair Kevin Warsh's latest meeting. Investors widely expect a rate increase in December as inflation tied to oil and gas price spikes persists.

items.headline: Netanyahu's rivals weigh support from Arab parties
items.summary: As Israelis await final results, opposition leaders are weighing whether to join forces with Arab parties to form a government. Arab citizens turned out strongly in the record-turnout vote.

items.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro arrives in the U.S. after Brazil loss
items.summary: Defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro arrived in the United States after refusing to concede. He faces Brazilian Supreme Court investigations over alleged financial crimes.

items.headline: Labor leader Dolores Huerta dies at 96
items.summary: Dolores Huerta, who co-founded the United Farm Workers union and coined the rallying cry 'Sí, se puede,' has died. She was a leading figure in the labor, feminist and civil rights movements.

items.headline: Administration moves to scrap methane rule
items.summary: The Trump administration wants to undo a Biden-era rule meant to cut methane emissions from the oil and gas industry. Methane is a potent planet-heating gas.

items.headline: El Niño expected to push carbon dioxide levels higher
items.summary: A new report warns that atmospheric carbon dioxide levels will surge this year amid a powerful El Niño. Yale Environment 360 reported the findings on Wednesday.

items.headline: Student voters' registration rights under scrutiny
items.summary: Advocates say many college students have the right to choose whether to register at school or at home, a right a Montana legal fight shows is misunderstood. Campus groups are organizing against Republican-led limits on youth ballot access.

items.headline: Cornell faculty vote on no-confidence measure
items.summary: Cornell faculty are set to vote on a no-confidence resolution against the university administration. The measure concerns its handling of a 2024 sexual assault report.

items.headline: How abortion bans are reshaping wider medical care
items.summary: In an interview about her book Side Effects, reporter Alice Miranda Ollstein describes how abortion bans affect care beyond reproductive health. The Nation published the conversation on Wednesday.

digest.overview:
The Federal Reserve held rates at 3.75% to 4% in a 10–2 vote, with two officials favoring a hike. A federal judge rejected the Justice Department's bid to make California set aside about 20,000 mail ballots from alleged noncitizens, and the department appealed. More than 35 million Americans have voted early, including a record 2 million-plus in-person voters in Georgia. Hackers knocked the Federal Election Commission's filing system offline days before the midterms. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, the Joint Chiefs' top planner, over alleged classified leaks. Utah filed criminal charges against prediction-market company Kalshi and its co-founders. The administration moved to scrap a Biden-era methane rule for oil and gas. Labor and civil rights leader Dolores Huerta died at 96.

Abroad, a high-speed train rear-ended a stopped train near Toledo, Spain, killing at least 68 people; officials blamed a signaling failure. With nearly 90% counted, Israel's Netanyahu bloc was on course for 53 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's for 48, with Arab parties at a record 19 and 61 needed. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said three tankers hit mines on an unauthorized Hormuz route, as President Trump denied peace talks are under way. The Kremlin said Europeans will not join U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi. Flávio Bolsonaro landed near Miami despite a Brazilian court order to surrender his passports. North Korea fired about a dozen short-range ballistic missiles, a week after Seoul offered military talks. A South Korean special counsel again sought the death penalty for former President Yoon Suk Yeol, and Samsung Electronics posted record quarterly profit. Cyclone Arnab struck India's Andhra Pradesh after 89,000 people were evacuated.

home.overview:
The Milwaukee Brewers are champions for the first time: they beat Tampa Bay 4–1 in Game 5 in St. Petersburg to take the World Series 4–1, as Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings and Jackson Chourio finished with a five-game Series record 11 hits; the parade is Friday. In the NBA, Stephen Curry dropped 44 in Golden State's 119–114 win at Minnesota, Victor Wembanyama posted 36 and 14 in an overtime win at Utah, Jalen Brunson scored 38 in the Knicks' 133–127 win in Chicago and Houston crushed Milwaukee 132–100, while Indiana lost Tyrese Haliburton week-to-week with a hamstring strain. The NFL's Week 8 opens tonight with Panthers at Packers.

Liverpool survived Chelsea 6–5 on penalties after a 1–1 draw and Man City got past Brighton 4–3 on penalties after 2–2 to reach the Carabao Cup quarterfinals, where Liverpool host Bournemouth and City host Bradford; Everton and Newcastle play tonight for a trip to Fleetwood. Saturday brings Der Klassiker in Munich and Chelsea vs. Man United, while K League 1's split round opens with Jeonbuk hosting Daejeon. In MLS, Philadelphia held Nashville 0–0 and New England climbed to second. In the KBO, Kia and Samsung play Game 3 tonight in Gwangju with their series tied 1–1 and a Korean Series date with KT Wiz on the line.

brief: Kia and Samsung play Game 3 of their best-of-five second round Thursday at 6:30 p.m. KST in Gwangju, with the series tied 1–1.
Keisho Shirakawa starts for Kia after holding LG to one run over five innings in the first-round clincher; Choi Won-tae starts for Samsung.
Kia manager Lee Bum-ho said he wants at least five innings from Shirakawa and is counting on lefty relievers Lee Eui-lee and Kwak Do-gyu against Samsung's left-heavy lineup.
Ariel Jurado earned his first KBO postseason win in Samsung's Game 2 victory.
The series winner faces regular-season champion KT Wiz in the Korean Series starting Nov. 2.

brief: Milwaukee beat Tampa Bay 4–1 in Game 5 on Wednesday to win the World Series 4–1, the first title in franchise history.
Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings before calf cramping cut his start short.
Rookie Cooper Pratt set a World Series rookie record with hits in six straight plate appearances and added a sacrifice fly for a 4–0 lead.
Jackson Chourio finished with 11 hits, a record for a five-game World Series, and Trevor Megill closed it after allowing a ninth-inning run.
Milwaukee's championship parade is Friday at 10 a.m. CT.
